To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Bt cotton hybrids MECH 162, MECH 164 and RCH 1 were highly toxic to neonates of H. armigeara.
the field population of H. armigere is highly susceptible to Bt cotton.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel approach to the study of the effect of different plant parts.
the development and implementation of new and innovative technologies for the production and protection of cotton.
the development of a new method to measure and predict the susceptibility of H. armigere larvae to Bt cotton in the field, based on their responses in the laboratory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Bt cotton has been effective in controlling cotton bollworm.
the susceptibility of H. armigerna populations in cotton fields to Bt cotton was not significantly different from the laboratory reared populations.
the susceptibility of H. armigear neonates to Bt cotton is high.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Bt hybrids are highly effective against H. armigeara neonates, but the efficacy decreases with the increase in larval instar and the efficacy also varies in different plant parts of the Bt hybrids.

there was no significant difference in susceptibility of laboratory and field populations of H. armigerna to three Bt hybrids, which was further confirmed by the fact that the susceptibility of H. armigena to three Bt hybrid was not affected by the age of larvae and plant parts.
the susceptibility of neonate larvae of H. armigere was higher than the older larvae.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Bt cotton hybrids are highly effective against H. armigara.
the efficacy of Bt hybrids in controlling H. armigerna was comparable to the laboratory selected population.
Bt cotton has been effective in reducing the incidence of H. armigere in cotton.
